claim: Little is known about the unusual dynamics of speck assembly.
source: This highlights the fact that we still know very little about the unusual dynamics of speck assembly, or the mystery why the cell normally always forms only one single speck.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge.

claim: It is a mystery why the cell normally always forms only one single speck.
source: This highlights the fact that we still know very little about the unusual dynamics of speck assembly, or the mystery why the cell normally always forms only one single speck.
evidence: This is a statement about an unexplained phenomenon.

claim: In response to Opto-ASC speck formation, periderm cells died in two morphologically different ways.
source: In response to the formation of an Opto-ASC speck periderm cells died in two morphologically different ways.
evidence: This is a summary of observations from imaging experiments.

claim: Apical extrusion of periderm cells has been described in response to infection.
source: Apical extrusion of periderm cells has been described not only in response to infection, but also in response to treatment with the antibiotic geneticin (G418) (Eisenhoffer and Rosenblatt, 2011) and during tissue homeostasis as a response to cell crowding (Eisenhoffer et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Eisenhoffer and Rosenblatt, 2011 and Eisenhoffer et al., 2012.

claim: Apical extrusion of periderm cells has been described in response to treatment with the antibiotic geneticin (G418).
source: Apical extrusion of periderm cells has been described not only in response to infection, but also in response to treatment with the antibiotic geneticin (G418) (Eisenhoffer and Rosenblatt, 2011) and during tissue homeostasis as a response to cell crowding (Eisenhoffer et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Eisenhoffer and Rosenblatt, 2011.

claim: Apical extrusion of periderm cells occurs during tissue homeostasis as a response to cell crowding.
source: Apical extrusion of periderm cells has been described not only in response to infection, but also in response to treatment with the antibiotic geneticin (G418) (Eisenhoffer and Rosenblatt, 2011) and during tissue homeostasis as a response to cell crowding (Eisenhoffer et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Eisenhoffer et al., 2012.

claim: Apoptotic stimuli like geneticin have been shown to induce extrusion via sphingosine-1 phosphate (S1P) and its receptor.
source: Apoptotic stimuli like geneticin have been shown to induce extrusion via sphingosine-1 phosphate (S1P) and its receptor, which is expressed in the surrounding cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge about extrusion mechanisms.

claim: S1P signaling does not seem to drive extrusion of pyroptotic cells in Caco-2 cell co-cultures.
source: We have previously shown that S1P signaling does not seem to drive extrusion of pyroptotic cells in Caco-2 cell co-cultures (Shkarina et al., 2022), but so far it is unclear if S1P signaling or another mechanism activated downstream of the inflammasome is responsible for apical extrusion.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Shkarina et al., 2022.

claim: It is unclear if S1P signaling or another mechanism activated downstream of the inflammasome is responsible for apical extrusion.
source: We have previously shown that S1P signaling does not seem to drive extrusion of pyroptotic cells in Caco-2 cell co-cultures (Shkarina et al., 2022), but so far it is unclear if S1P signaling or another mechanism activated downstream of the inflammasome is responsible for apical extrusion.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge.

claim: The factors determining the direction of extrusion remain to be discovered.
source: Although the factors determining the direction of extrusion remain to be discovered, the different ratios of apical and basal extrusion of periderm cells in different zebrafish strains suggest a genetic component.
evidence: This is a statement about what is not yet known.

claim: The different ratios of apical and basal extrusion in different zebrafish strains suggest a genetic component.
source: Although the factors determining the direction of extrusion remain to be discovered, the different ratios of apical and basal extrusion of periderm cells in different zebrafish strains suggest a genetic component.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation of strain-specific differences.

claim: Different types of cell death are not entirely separable, but represent different manifestations of parallel and interconnected signaling pathways.
source: These findings indicate that different types of cell death are not entirely separable, but that they represent different manifestations of parallel and interconnected signaling pathways, the overall balance of which defines the final outcomes.
evidence: This is an inference from the observations of overlapping phenotypes.

claim: The overall balance of parallel and interconnected signaling pathways defines the final outcomes of cell death.
source: These findings indicate that different types of cell death are not entirely separable, but that they represent different manifestations of parallel and interconnected signaling pathways, the overall balance of which defines the final outcomes.
evidence: This is an inference from the observations of overlapping phenotypes.

claim: Disrupting one cell death pathway directs the cell towards a different pathway that may have a different phenotypic outcome.
source: This is also evident from other studies in the past, where disrupting one pathway directs the cell towards a different pathway that may have a different phenotypic outcome (Tsuchiya et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tsuchiya et al., 2019.

claim: A 'pure' phenotype can only be induced through experimental activation of the most downstream effector.
source: Perhaps it is only through experimental activation of the most downstream effector that a 'pure' phenotype can be induced.
evidence: This is speculation about how to achieve specific phenotypes.

claim: Caspb is essential for apical extrusion in zebrafish periderm.
source: In the case of zebrafish periderm, we identified Caspb as essential for apical extrusion.
evidence: This is a finding from caspb knockout experiments.

claim: In the absence of Caspb, cells die with an apoptotic morphology in response to speck formation.
source: In the absence of Caspb, cells die with an apoptotic morphology in response to speck formation.
evidence: This is a finding from caspb knockout experiments.

claim: The requirement for Caspb for apical extrusion and lysis might explain the difference in response to ASC-speck formation between periderm and basal cells.
source: The requirement for Caspb for apical extrusion and lysis might also explain the difference in the response to ASC-speck formation between the periderm and the underlying basal cells.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism underlying cell-type differences.

claim: According to cell-type-specific RNA sequencing data, basal cells express ten times lower levels of Caspb than periderm cells.
source: According to cell-type-specific RNA sequencing data (Cokus et al., 2019), basal cells express ten times lower levels of Caspb than periderm cells.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Cokus et al., 2019.

claim: Caspa was not found to be necessary for speck induced extrusion.
source: Although Caspa localizes to the ASC speck (Kuri et al., 2017) and is necessary for rapid cell death if no Caspb is present, we did not find it to be necessary for speck induced extrusion.
evidence: This is a finding from caspa knockout experiments.

claim: The delay between speck formation and cell death in Caspa deficient cells can be partially explained by the type of cell imaged, namely basal cells.
source: We have now re-analyzed our previous data (Figure 7—figure supplement 2) and found that the delay between speck formation and cell death can be partially explained by the type of cell that was imaged, namely basal cells, although we observed a much stronger delay between speck formation and cell death in Caspa deficient cells than in wildtype basal cells.
evidence: This is a finding from re-analysis of previous data.

claim: Zebrafish Caspa and Caspb are redundant in their role as rapid cell death inducers.
source: Zebrafish Caspa and Caspb are thus redundant in their role as rapid cell death inducers, but the downstream mechanisms that lead to either extrusion or apoptosis of periderm cells are yet to be identified.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that either caspase alone can induce death.

claim: The downstream mechanisms that lead to either extrusion or apoptosis of periderm cells are yet to be identified.
source: Zebrafish Caspa and Caspb are thus redundant in their role as rapid cell death inducers, but the downstream mechanisms that lead to either extrusion or apoptosis of periderm cells are yet to be identified.
evidence: This is a statement about what is not yet known.

claim: In Caco-2 cell monolayers caspase-1 causes pyroptosis with rapid apical extrusion and a lamellipodial response in neighbouring cells which close the wound within approximately 70 min.
source: For example, in Caco-2 cell monolayers caspase-1 causes pyroptosis with rapid apical extrusion and a lamellipodial response in neighbouring cells which close the wound within approximately 70 min (Bonfim-Melo et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bonfim-Melo et al., 2022.

claim: Wound closure after ASC-induced apical extrusion of zebrafish periderm cells is much faster (around 10 min) than in Caco-2 cells.
source: Wound closure after ASC-induced apical extrusion of zebrafish periderm cells is much faster (around 10 min).
evidence: This is a comparative finding from imaging experiments.

claim: Basal cells trigger a lamellipodial response in neighbouring cells and take longer to close the gap.
source: Basal cells on the other hand trigger a lamellipodial response in neighbouring cells and take longer to close the gap (Figure 6—figure supplement 3B), similar to Caco-2 cells.
evidence: This is an observation from imaging experiments.

claim: Apoptosis and ASC-induced cell death are both initiated within a short time after speck formation.
source: Apoptosis and ASC-induced cell death are both initiated within a short time after speck formation and cause the recruitment of actin in surrounding periderm cells to the side facing the dying cells.
evidence: This is an observation from imaging experiments.

claim: Apoptosis and ASC-induced cell death cause the recruitment of actin in surrounding periderm cells to the side facing the dying cells.
source: Apoptosis and ASC-induced cell death are both initiated within a short time after speck formation and cause the recruitment of actin in surrounding periderm cells to the side facing the dying cells.
evidence: This is an observation from actin imaging experiments.

claim: The closure of the surrounding epithelium is faster for ASC-induced extrusion than for apoptosis.
source: The closure of the surrounding epithelium above or below the extruded cell is faster for ASC-induced extrusion than for apoptosis.
evidence: This is a comparative finding from time-lapse imaging experiments.

claim: The difference in rate of wound closure could be caused by different dynamics in the cell itself, or in the surrounding cells.
source: This difference in rate of wound closure could be caused by different dynamics in the cell itself, or in the surrounding cells.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism underlying the difference.

claim: An immediate Ca2+ response occurs in the case of ASC-induced death, but not apoptosis.
source: The fact that we observe an immediate Ca2+ response in the case of ASC-induced death, but not apoptosis, indicates signalling from the dying cell to the surrounding epithelium, and this signal differs between cells dying apoptotically or by ASC-induced death.
evidence: This is an observation from calcium imaging experiments.

claim: The Ca2+ signal differs between cells dying apoptotically or by ASC-induced death.
source: The fact that we observe an immediate Ca2+ response in the case of ASC-induced death, but not apoptosis, indicates signalling from the dying cell to the surrounding epithelium, and this signal differs between cells dying apoptotically or by ASC-induced death.
evidence: This is an inference from calcium imaging observations.

claim: Caspase-8-induced apical extrusion of MDCK cells is preceded by a strong calcium wave in surrounding cells.
source: Caspase-8-induced apical extrusion of MDCK cells is preceded by a strong calcium wave in surrounding cells (Takeuchi et al., 2020), further suggesting that the Ca2+ wave correlates with the mode of extrusion rather than the trigger for cell death.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Takeuchi et al., 2020.

claim: The Ca2+ wave correlates with the mode of extrusion rather than the trigger for cell death.
source: Caspase-8-induced apical extrusion of MDCK cells is preceded by a strong calcium wave in surrounding cells (Takeuchi et al., 2020), further suggesting that the Ca2+ wave correlates with the mode of extrusion rather than the trigger for cell death.
evidence: This is an inference from comparing different cell death modes.

claim: The fast apical extrusion and the rapid Ca2+ response require Caspb.
source: The fast apical extrusion and the rapid Ca2+ response require Caspb, pointing to a Caspb-dependent signalling event.
evidence: This is a finding from caspb knockout experiments.

claim: A Caspb-dependent signalling event is involved in fast apical extrusion and rapid Ca2+ response.
source: The fast apical extrusion and the rapid Ca2+ response require Caspb, pointing to a Caspb-dependent signalling event.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that these processes require Caspb.

claim: A bacterial infection sensed by the NAIP/NLRC4 inflammasome induces a fast myosin-dependent contraction in surrounding cells in cultured intestinal epithelial cells.
source: A similar reaction was observed in cultured intestinal epithelial cells in which a bacterial infection sensed by the NAIP/NLRC4 inflammasome induce a fast myosin-dependent contraction in surrounding cells.
evidence: This is a statement about findings in another system.

claim: The myosin-dependent contraction in surrounding cells was dependent on the activation of sub-lytic GSDMD pores and the resulting ion flux.
source: This reaction was dependent on the activation of sub-lytic GSDMD pores and the resulting ion flux and independent of the cell death or extrusion of the cell (Samperio Ventayol et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Samperio Ventayol et al., 2021.

claim: The myosin-dependent contraction in surrounding cells was independent of the cell death or extrusion of the cell.
source: This reaction was dependent on the activation of sub-lytic GSDMD pores and the resulting ion flux and independent of the cell death or extrusion of the cell (Samperio Ventayol et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Samperio Ventayol et al., 2021.

claim: Zebrafish do not have a direct homolog of GsdmD but two homologues of GsdmE (Gsdmea/b).
source: Zebrafish do not have a direct homolog of GsdmD but two homologues of GsdmE (Gsdmea/b).
evidence: This is established knowledge about zebrafish gasdermins.

claim: Human GsdmE is activated downstream of caspase-3 during apoptosis.
source: Human GsdmE is activated downstream of caspase-3 during apoptosis (Wang et al., 2017) and it plays a role in the caspase-3-mediated lytic death of primary human keratinocytes after viral inactivation of the Bcl-2 pathway (Orzalli et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2017.

claim: Human GsdmE plays a role in the caspase-3-mediated lytic death of primary human keratinocytes after viral inactivation of the Bcl-2 pathway.
source: Human GsdmE is activated downstream of caspase-3 during apoptosis (Wang et al., 2017) and it plays a role in the caspase-3-mediated lytic death of primary human keratinocytes after viral inactivation of the Bcl-2 pathway (Orzalli et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Orzalli et al., 2021.

claim: Both zebrafish gasdermins can be cleaved by Caspb and other apoptotic caspases (but not Caspa) in vitro.
source: Both zebrafish gasdermins can be cleaved by Caspb and other apoptotic caspases (but not Caspa) in vitro (Chen et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Chen et al., 2021.

claim: No change in peridermal keratinocyte cell death was seen after ASC-speck formation when Gsdme a and b were knocked out by CRISPR/Cas9.
source: It was therefore surprising to find that we did not see a change in peridermal keratinocyte cell death after ASC-speck formation when we knocked out Gsdme a and b by CRISPR/Cas9.
evidence: This is a finding from GSDM knockout experiments.

claim: Gsdme a and b may be redundant in their function to mediate Caspb dependent extrusion and a small amount may be sufficient to induce this form of cell death.
source: Although the CRISPR/Cas 9 strategy is highly efficient, and in our hands has worked well for other genes, we cannot rule out that Gsdme a and b are redundant in their function to mediate Caspb dependent extrusion and that a small amount is sufficient to induce this form of cell death.
evidence: This is speculation about why GSDM knockout had no effect.

claim: Cells which are extruded do not lyse immediately upon swelling.
source: Additionally, we find that cells which are extruded do not lyse immediately upon swelling which is normally the case in pyroptotic cultured cells (Shkarina et al., 2022).
evidence: This is an observation from imaging experiments.

claim: A Caspb-dependent difference in cell death phenotypes exists.
source: Since we find a Caspb-dependent difference in cell death phenotypes, the question arises which other components could cause the apical extrusion of cells and the wave-like Ca2+ signaling response in surrounding cells.
evidence: This is a finding from caspb knockout experiments.

claim: Pannexins, especially pannexin1a, could be candidates for causing apical extrusion and Ca2+ signaling.
source: Possible candidates could be pannexins, especially pannexin1a, which is expressed in skin cells (Cokus et al., 2019) and is necessary downstream of caspase-11 to induce pyroptosis in response to LPS in mouse macrophages (Yang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is speculation about alternative mechanisms supported by citations.

claim: Pannexin1a is expressed in skin cells.
source: Possible candidates could be pannexins, especially pannexin1a, which is expressed in skin cells (Cokus et al., 2019) and is necessary downstream of caspase-11 to induce pyroptosis in response to LPS in mouse macrophages (Yang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Cokus et al., 2019.

claim: Pannexin1a is necessary downstream of caspase-11 to induce pyroptosis in response to LPS in mouse macrophages.
source: Possible candidates could be pannexins, especially pannexin1a, which is expressed in skin cells (Cokus et al., 2019) and is necessary downstream of caspase-11 to induce pyroptosis in response to LPS in mouse macrophages (Yang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yang et al., 2015.

claim: The release of ATP caused by pannexin pores might explain the strong calcium wave in the Caspb-dependent extrusion of peridermal keratinocytes.
source: The release of ATP caused by pannexin pores might explain the strong calcium wave in the Caspb-dependent extrusion of peridermal keratinocytes (Mori et al., 2022).
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism supported by citation to Mori et al., 2022.
